skill.name: container-grype
skill.description: Guides Grype scans for container images, filesystems, and SBOMs. Provides CI examples, severity gates, report formats, and CVSS, EPSS, and CISA KEV prioritization.
skill.summary: Scan container artifacts with Grype and prioritize actionable vulnerabilities.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, defensive examples, and normal Grype configuration. Confirmed risks include unpinned pipe-to-shell installers, Docker socket exposure, and unquoted Tekton parameters that permit command injection. Semantic review also found bypassable security gates, broad ignore rules, and mutable CI dependencies.

remediation.issue: Remote installers are piped directly into shell interpreters.
remediation.suggestion: Download a versioned release, verify its published checksum or signature, and execute only the verified local file.

remediation.issue: The Jenkins example exposes the host Docker socket to the scanner container.
remediation.suggestion: Scan a registry image or SBOM without the socket, or use an isolated rootless builder with narrowly scoped access.

remediation.issue: Tekton parameters are inserted into shell commands without quoting or validation.
remediation.suggestion: Pass parameters through environment variables, quote every expansion, and validate image references and severity values against strict allowlists.

remediation.issue: CI examples use mutable action branches and latest container tags.
remediation.suggestion: Pin actions to reviewed commit SHAs and container images to immutable digests or exact release versions.

remediation.issue: Some scanner failures and findings do not fail the pipeline.
remediation.suggestion: Remove unconditional success handling, parse every scanner result, and enforce documented severity thresholds before deployment.

remediation.issue: The example Grype configuration contains broad active ignore rules.
remediation.suggestion: Comment out sample ignores and require exact CVE, package, justification, owner, and expiration details for every suppression.

semantic_findings.title: Security gates can pass without enforcing findings
semantic_findings.description: Node audit output is never evaluated, and the IaC stage converts scanner failures into warnings. Vulnerable builds can pass despite the template presenting these checks as gates.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Node command is followed by no result check, while the IaC block uses || true and leaves exit 1 commented out.

semantic_findings.title: Example configuration suppresses broad vulnerability classes
semantic_findings.description: The bundled Grype configuration ignores every wont-fix vulnerability and all matches for a named package. Copying it can hide real findings without expiry or target-specific justification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The active ignore rules include fix-state: wont-fix and a package-only pytest match, both broader than the example-specific CVE suppressions.

semantic_findings.title: CI examples execute mutable action and image references
semantic_findings.description: The templates use a GitHub Action from master and Grype container images tagged latest. Future upstream changes can execute without repository review or digest verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly reference aquasecurity/trivy-action@master, set GRYPE_VERSION to latest, and run anchore/grype:latest.

content.value_statement: Container findings are difficult to rank across severity, exploitability, and exposure. This skill guides Grype scans and practical remediation priorities.
actual_capabilities: Guides Grype scans for container images, local filesystems, and SBOM files.
Explains table, JSON, SARIF, CycloneDX, and custom template outputs.
Provides CI examples for GitHub Actions, GitLab, Jenkins, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, and Tekton.
Prioritizes findings with CVSS severity, EPSS probability, and CISA KEV status.
Documents ignore rules, database management, exclusions, and severity thresholds.
limitations: Requires Grype and access to the selected image, filesystem, or SBOM.
Database updates and remote image scans may require network access and registry credentials.
Does not patch vulnerable packages or validate that a remediation preserves application behavior.
References helper scripts that are not included in the published file structure.

use_cases.title: Prioritize remediation work
use_cases.description: Rank package findings using KEV status, EPSS probability, CVSS severity, and fix availability.

use_cases.title: Assess software inventories
use_cases.description: Scan archived SPDX, CycloneDX, or Syft SBOMs without rebuilding container images.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the safest Grype command to scan [image]. Explain each option and use a production severity threshold.

prompt_templates.title: Review scan findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Grype report summary: [findings]. Rank the issues by KEV, EPSS, CVSS, fix availability, and package exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Grype gate for [CI platform] scanning [image source]. Pin dependencies and retain reports without exposing the Docker socket.

prompt_templates.title: Build a remediation program
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a remediation plan for [portfolio]. Define SLAs, exception evidence, expiry rules, rescan checks, and metrics for KEV and high-EPSS findings.

output_examples.input: Prioritize three findings: a KEV high, a critical with low EPSS, and a medium with high EPSS.
output_examples.output: Priority 1 is the KEV high because exploitation is confirmed. Priority 2 is the high-EPSS medium. Priority 3 is the low-EPSS critical.

output_examples.input: Recommend a production gate for a container image.
output: Block releases with critical or high findings that have available fixes.
Escalate every CISA KEV finding regardless of CVSS score.
Store SARIF and human-readable reports as restricted build artifacts.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a Grype ignore rule is acceptable.
output_examples.output: Accept the rule only with exact scope, evidence, an owner, an expiration date, and a scheduled rescan. Avoid package-wide or fix-state-wide suppressions.

best_practices: Pin scanner actions, images, and installers to reviewed immutable versions.
Prioritize KEV and high-EPSS findings before relying only on CVSS severity.
Document every suppression with evidence, ownership, expiration, and periodic review.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installer content directly into a shell.
Do not mount the host Docker socket when an image or SBOM scan is sufficient.
Do not ignore scanner exit codes without enforcing equivalent result checks.

faq.question: What targets can Grype scan?
faq.answer: Grype can scan container images, local directories, image archives, and supported SBOM documents.

faq.question: Does this skill install Grype?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and pipeline examples. Install a pinned Grype release through a verified package or artifact.

faq.question: Can it scan without Docker access?
faq.answer: Yes. Scan registry images, image archives, directories, or SBOMs when Docker socket access is unavailable or inappropriate.

faq.question: How should findings be prioritized?
faq.answer: Address CISA KEV findings first, then high-EPSS issues, critical CVSS findings, and high CVSS findings with reachable vulnerable code.

faq.question: Which report format should I use?
faq.answer: Use table output for review, SARIF for code platforms, JSON for automation, and CycloneDX for compatible supply chain tools.

faq.question: When is an ignore rule acceptable?
faq.answer: Use one only after validating impact and recording exact scope, evidence, ownership, expiration, and a future review date.
